summary:
ASTROCARE is an astronaut health monitoring dashboard, built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It tracks six simulated vitals in real time: heart rate, oxygen, temperature, blood pressure, cabin carbon dioxide, and sleep. Each reading turns green, yellow, or red against medical limits, and any danger triggers a flashing emergency banner, an alarm, and a timestamped alert log.

It addresses the challenge by watching astronaut health continuously, warning instantly when a value crosses a safe limit, and monitoring radiation dose with a clear shelter instruction. A live heart rate chart shows trends, reminders support hydration and exercise, and a built-in search opens real NASA OSDR space biology studies.

It matters because astronauts are far from doctors, and early warning can prevent small problems from becoming emergencies. It works on laptops and phones, and its data is simulated, designed to grow into real sensor integration.
details:
What it does and how it works: ASTROCARE is a web dashboard that monitors an astronaut’s health. Every 2 seconds it generates simulated readings for heart rate, oxygen, temperature, blood pressure, cabin carbon dioxide, and sleep, plus radiation dose rate and total mission dose. Each value is checked against medical limits that can be edited in the code. Cards turn green for normal, yellow for warning, and red for danger. A danger reading triggers a flashing emergency banner, an alarm sound, and a timestamped entry in the alert log. If radiation becomes dangerous, the app tells the astronaut to move to the shielded shelter.

Benefits and impact: Astronauts are far from doctors, so early warning matters. The app helps catch problems before they become emergencies, supports healthy habits with hydration reminders, an exercise tracker, and wellness tips, and shows heart rate trends in a live chart. A built-in search connects users to real studies in the NASA Open Science Data Repository.

Tools used: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, written in Visual Studio Code, with Chart.js for the live chart. It runs in any browser on a laptop or phone, with no installation. AI assistants were used to help write and debug code.

Creativity: The app combines vitals, radiation protection, healthy-habit support, and NASA research access in one simple dashboard, with a one-click Test Emergency Alert for demonstrations.

Factors considered: Clear alerts that are easy to read in an emergency, a layout that works on small screens, and honesty about data. All readings are simulated for education, and this is not a medical device. Future work includes real wearable sensors, live OSDR data, and PDF reports for flight surgeons.
